concepts.title: Braking systems
concepts.summary: How rider input becomes braking torque at the wheel, and why controls, calipers, rotors, tires and surface grip must be understood as one system.
principles: Brake controls command force; calipers and rotors create braking torque at the wheel.
Available deceleration also depends on tire grip, load transfer and surface conditions.
Rotor, caliper, pad, control and fluid/cable compatibility remain component-specific.

componentTargets.note: Performance-road disc brake implementation.
Trail braking designed around repeated off-road control demands.
Everyday utility braking within an all-weather platform.
All-road braking across changing surfaces.

concepts.title: Tire volume, pressure & contact
concepts.summary: How tire dimensions, pressure, casing, load and surface conditions shape support, compliance, traction and rolling behavior.
principles: Nominal tire width alone cannot determine correct pressure.
More volume generally broadens the usable support/compliance range but does not remove tire/rim limits.
Road, trail, utility and gravel tires optimize different mixtures of rolling efficiency, grip, durability and comfort.

componentTargets.note: Narrow performance-road tire lineage.
High-volume trail tire for traction and impact control.
Medium-volume utility tire balancing comfort and everyday efficiency.
Mixed-surface tire balancing pavement and loose-surface requirements.

concepts.title: Chain drive & power transmission
concepts.summary: How crank torque travels through chainrings, chain and rear gearing to drive the rear wheel across derailleur and internal-hub architectures.
principles: The chain transmits torque between front and rear rotating elements.
Derailleur systems change the external chain path across multiple sprockets.
Internal-gear systems can keep one external rear sprocket while changing ratios inside the hub.

componentTargets.note: Multi-chainring road derailleur power path.
1× trail drivetrain under rough-surface use.
Protected external chain feeding an internal-gear hub.
1× all-road power path into a wide cassette.

concepts.title: Gearing, range & shifting
concepts.summary: How bicycles trade ratio range, gear steps, simplicity, exposure and control architecture to match different terrain and use cases.
principles: Gear ratio changes the relationship between crank rotation and rear-wheel rotation.
Road, 1× off-road, 1× gravel and internal-hub systems distribute their ratios differently.
Shifter, rear mechanism, sprocket range, chain and mounting interfaces must belong to compatible systems.

componentTargets.note: Closely stepped performance-road rear ratios.
Wide-range trail 1× gearing.
Ratios packaged inside the rear hub.
Wide-range 1× all-road gearing.

concepts.title: Steering, geometry & control
concepts.summary: How frame geometry, fork, headset, cockpit, rider position and tire contact combine to shape steering response and stability.
principles: The handlebar is the rider interface, but steering behavior comes from the entire front-end and chassis geometry.
Wheelbase, head angle, reach, stack and rider position create different handling priorities.
Road, trail, upright utility and gravel bikes deliberately place the rider and front wheel differently.

componentTargets.note: Performance-road geometry and low aerodynamic position.
Trail geometry prioritizing terrain control.
Swept cockpit supporting upright everyday control.
Flared drops add mixed-surface hand positions and leverage.

concepts.title: Suspension & compliance
concepts.summary: How bicycles absorb terrain through tires, rider movement, frame/fork behavior and—on dedicated off-road machines—spring and damping systems.
principles: Suspension separates wheel movement from chassis movement through spring and damping elements.
Rigid bicycles still gain compliance from tires, contact points, structure and rider movement.
Travel, sag, spring rate and damping are suspension-system specific rather than universal bicycle settings.

componentTargets.note: Dedicated front suspension for trail impacts and control.
Rear spring/damper controlling chassis-wheel motion.
Rigid all-road compliance relies heavily on tire volume.
Utility comfort without dedicated suspension travel.

concepts.title: Wheels, hubs & axles
concepts.summary: How rims, spokes, hubs, bearings and axles form rotating structures that carry load while locating tires, brakes and drivetrain interfaces.
principles: The wheel is a load-carrying structure, not just a tire holder.
Hub architecture can carry bearings, brake rotors, freehub mechanisms or internal gears.
Axle and hub interfaces must match the frame or fork that locates the wheel.

componentTargets.note: Road freehub and cassette interface.
Trail wheel built around impact and terrain loads.
Wheel hub also contains the transmission.
All-road rim supporting a higher-volume mixed-surface tire.

concepts.title: Cargo, mounts & utility hardware
concepts.summary: How racks, bosses, fork mounts and everyday equipment attach loads to the bicycle while changing structural demands and handling.
principles: A mounting interface does not reveal its allowable load by appearance alone.
The lowest applicable frame, fork, rack, fastener or accessory limit governs the real setup.
Cargo position influences steering, braking, parking stability and wheel/accessory clearance.

componentTargets.note: Dedicated everyday rear cargo structure.
Parking support interacting with loaded-bike stability.
Frame attachment points for compatible all-road luggage.
Fork mounts that add steering-sensitive cargo possibilities.

concepts.title: Frame architecture & rider position
concepts.summary: How frame form, stack, reach, contact points and intended environment create distinct performance, trail, utility and all-road riding positions.
principles: Frame architecture establishes where major components and rider contact points can be placed.
Rider position is an outcome of frame geometry plus cockpit, saddle and fit—not one dimension alone.
Step-through access, aggressive road posture, trail control and all-road balance are different optimization targets.

componentTargets.note: Performance-road chassis and rider-position foundation.
Full-suspension trail chassis.
Step-through utility architecture.
All-road chassis between road and trail priorities.
